title: The Spoon Holder's Revenge
title_candidates: The Easiest Hole on the Course
Mullin: From Last to First in Kent
theme: The man who had made a second home of last place arrived in Kent as a Trophy afterthought and left holding both the Trophy and the Jacket — because the man best-placed to stop him handed it back on the easiest hole on the course.
opening_hook: Open at the moment the tournament was decided: Alex Baker, two points behind Mullin entering the final holes at Prince's in R4, playing the 16th — par 4, rated SI17, the easiest hole on the course — and running up a 10. Then step back and explain how Mullin, three-time reigning Spoon holder, came to be the man Baker needed to overhaul.
foreshadow: Mullin carries three consecutive Wooden Spoons into Kent — the last man in the field you would back to lift the Trophy come Sunday.
Alex Baker's habit of spectacular blow-ups: two holes wiped out at Royal Cinque Ports in R1 signal how this week will work when concentration lapses.
Jon Baker, defending Trophy champion and double Jacket holder, settles to the bottom of the standings on only the 4th hole of the tournament — an omen dressed as a blip.
Prince's plays twice: R3 and R4 on the same Shore/Dunes layout, so the course will have the final word.

competitions.name: Trophy
competitions.how: Led wire-to-wire from R1 H16, banking two best-in-field Stableford rounds (40 and 41 pts) to open a 9-point cushion by R2; survived Baker's R3-R4 comeback — Baker outplayed him in both rounds — because Baker's sextuple bogey at H16 R4 (b01, SI17) surrendered 7 points in a single hole, ending the chase and converting a near-flip into a 6-point Mullin win.

competitions.name: Green Jacket
competitions.how: Genuinely built: best-in-field on gross in R1 (87, a personal best at Royal Cinque Ports) and R2 (85, a personal best at Littlestone), opening a 12-shot lead by R2 that became a 7-shot winning margin; Jon Baker, the back-to-back defending Jacket champion, was never within range.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Baker dropped to last on H4 R1 and never left: bottom of the field in 2 of 4 rounds, 12 points adrift of Williams; even an ordinary R3 instead of his worst wouldn't have changed the outcome. R4 course record at Prince's (cr01) was the brilliant consolation prize for a week that was over before lunch on day one.

headline_candidates: The Easiest Hole on the Course Does the Impossible
SI 17, a Sextuple, and a Trophy That Changed Hands Then Changed Back
Jon Baker Sets a Course Record on His Way to the Spoon
rounds.chosen_headline: The Easiest Hole on the Course Does the Impossible
rounds.angle: Baker needs to overhaul a 2-point deficit and plays the back nine brilliantly — then runs up a 10 on H16 (par 4, SI17) to blow 7 points in one act of calamity; Mullin's own quad at H10 (b06) had briefly opened the door, but Baker walked in and then shut it himself; Jon Baker's consolation course record at Prince's (cr01) puts the coda on an upside-down week.

players.arc: Three consecutive Wooden Spoons going in; left Kent with the Trophy and Jacket double — the least likely man in the field who turned out to be the only one still standing when Baker handed it over on H16.
Outplayed the champion in R3 and R4, clawed within 2 points with three holes to play — and gave it back on the easiest hole on the course, on a par 4 rated SI17.
Arrived as defending Trophy champion and double Jacket holder; left with the Spoon and a course record — a week that was simultaneously R4 brilliance and 72-hole catastrophe.
Posted a personal-best gross total in a week where he was never in either race — the quiet witness to someone else's story.

venue_notes: TEG's 2nd visit to Kent across four links rounds: Royal Cinque Ports (2nd TEG visit) sets the tone as a formidable Open venue; Littlestone on Romney Marshes (2nd visit) is where the Jacket became unassailable; Prince's Shore/Dunes (2nd and 3rd visits, R3 and R4) is where the tournament was both nearly overturned and finally settled. Use the two-day Prince's residency as the Act 2/3 hinge — the same course hosted Mullin's R3 wobble and R4's decisive hole. Thread the remote, wind-exposed links character of Kent throughout; all four courses test the same skills, which makes Mullin's three personal bests across the week the more striking.

Trophy: Mullin led wire-to-wire; the only genuine threat arrived in R4 when Baker's back-nine charge closed the gap to 2 with three holes left.
The win is 'inherited' by anatomy: Baker outplayed Mullin in R3 and R4, but the 9-point bank built in R1-R2 was what held — not R3-R4 form.

Baker's sextuple at H16 R4 (b01, SI17 — the easiest hole on the course) forfeited 7 Stableford points and converted a potential Baker Trophy into a Mullin one; even a routine bogey there and Baker wins.
Mullin was the field's most consistent man despite two rounds in the bottom half — the architecture of a Trophy won in the first two days and defended by one hole.
Green Jacket: Mullin's Jacket was built, not gifted: best in field on gross in R1 (87 at Royal Cinque Ports, personal best) and R2 (85 at Littlestone, personal best), opening a 12-shot lead.
Jon Baker, back-to-back defending Jacket champion, was 7 shots behind at the end and never within range — the biggest reversal of roles in any competition this week.
Mullin set course personal bests at all three venues; the Jacket margin reflects genuine ball-striking dominance, not borrowed luck.
Wooden Spoon: Jon Baker dropped to last on H4 of R1 (b48) and occupied that position for all 72 holes — the defending Trophy champion's total collapse.
The 12-point margin to Williams was built by Baker: worse than Williams in 2 of 4 rounds, last in the field in 2 of 4 rounds; the outcome was never in doubt.
Even with an ordinary R3 instead of his worst (28 pts), Baker would still have taken the Spoon — the gap was too large for one improved round to bridge.
Baker's R4 39-point round and course record at Prince's provide the week's bittersweet footnote: the best golf of his week came when the Spoon was long since his.

David Mullin: 2 prior Trophy wins, 8 prior Jacket wins — but 4 Spoons total, 3 consecutive going into TEG 14; the reigning Spoon holder arrives as the field's form disaster.
R1 (40 pts, best in field at Royal Cinque Ports) and R2 (41 pts, best in field at Littlestone) — two consecutive best-in-field Stableford rounds, the only player to manage that across the week.
R3 wobble (9 on H8 at Prince's, b15) trimmed his Trophy lead from 9 to 8; he steadied with a 10-hole clean run on the back nine including a closing birdie (b17).
R4: last in the field for the round (37 pts) but the banked lead held; Baker did everything right until H16.
Alex Baker: 1 prior Trophy win, 1 prior Spoon — the man with the range to beat Mullin if his round held together for 18 consecutive holes.
Pattern of spectacular blow-ups runs all week: quintuple at H16 R1 (b23), quad at H11 R1 (b31), two quads in R2 (b24, b27), quad at H10 R3 (b14).
R4 up to H15: outplaying Mullin, scoring 2 points better on the back nine — within 2 points of the lead with three holes remaining.
H16 R4 (SI17, the easiest hole on the course): 10 gross, 0 Stableford points; the sextuple converted a potential Trophy win into a Mullin title in one swing.
Jon Baker: Defending Trophy champion (TEG 13) and back-to-back Jacket holder going in — the biggest fall of the week in any competition.
Last in the Trophy standings from H4 R1 through the final putt; 12 points adrift of Williams, the next-worst.

R4: 39 Stableford (best of his week by 11 points) and a course record at Prince's (83 gross, beating the prior record of 85 across 5 visits, cr01) — produced his finest golf when it could no longer help.
The Spoon was his regardless of an improved R3; the margin was too large and the week was effectively over at lunchtime on day one.
Gregg Williams: 3 prior Trophy wins, finished 3rd — never threatening the top nor the bottom, always occupying the gap between two more dramatic stories.
Personal-best gross total (+76, b25) was the week's quiet achievement on a Trophy that offered him no route to the podium.

course_history_notes: David Mullin set personal bests at all three venues: Royal Cinque Ports (87 gross, down 7 from his 94 in TEG 13), Littlestone (85, down 7 from 92), Prince's (91, down 1 from 92) — the best links week of his TEG career.

Jon Baker was 13 shots worse at Littlestone than TEG 13 (92 vs 79) and 7 shots worse at Royal Cinque Ports (92 vs 85) — the first two venues that buried his Trophy defence before Prince's could decide it.
Gregg Williams was 11 shots worse at Littlestone than TEG 13 (97 vs 86) — the course that made the Jacket unassailable by the end of R2.

Jon Baker's R4 course record at Prince's (83 gross, beating the prior record of 85 set across 5 visits, cr01) is the week's finest single gross round — set during a Spoon week by the defending Trophy champion.
decisive_moments: Trophy: Alex Baker's sextuple bogey at Prince's H16 R4 (SI17, the easiest hole on the course) — 7 Stableford points surrendered in a single act, converting a 2-point Baker deficit into a 6-point Mullin victory.
Green Jacket: Mullin's R1 and R2 at Royal Cinque Ports and Littlestone — back-to-back best-in-field gross rounds opened a 12-shot lead that the field was never equipped to chase down.
Wooden Spoon: R1 H4 at Royal Cinque Ports — Jon Baker, the defending Trophy champion, settled to last place four holes into the tournament and never once escaped it across the remaining 68 holes.

payoffs.seed: Mullin carries three consecutive Wooden Spoons into Kent
payoffs.payoff: Mullin wins both wire-to-wire — the serial Spoon holder claims both prizes and erases three years of last-place finishes in four days on the Kent coast.

payoffs.seed: Alex Baker's pattern of spectacular blow-ups from R1
payoffs.payoff: The sextuple at H16 (SI17) is the week's decisive blow — the pattern that ran through R1, R2, and R3 collects its final toll at the worst possible moment, on the easiest hole on the course.

payoffs.seed: Jon Baker drops to last on H4 R1 — the defending champion's fall begins immediately
payoffs.payoff: Baker occupies bottom place for all 72 holes; his R4 course record is the brilliant consolation for a week that was decided against him before lunchtime on day one.

payoffs.seed: Prince's plays twice — the course that will have the final word
payoffs.payoff: Both of R4's defining moments happen at Prince's: Baker's sextuple on the easiest hole and Jon Baker's course record — the same course that witnessed Mullin's R3 wobble delivers the tournament's resolution.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Mullin's 3-consecutive-Spoon background is genuinely the most interesting context for his Trophy win and pairs naturally with the hard-rule counterfactual; both are in narrative_vehicles, with inversion added for the defending-champion-takes-the-Spoon arc.

why_the_champion_won: Mullin banked two best-in-field rounds in R1 and R2 to build a 9-point Trophy cushion — an 'inherited' win in the sense that Baker outplayed him in R3 and R4, but Baker's sextuple at H16 R4 (SI17) gave back more than the entire R3-R4 swing had earned; Mullin was the man who was there to take what his rival surrendered on the easiest hole on the course.
